summary: Nora can tell who is in an Instagram group. Asking "who's here" answers instead of refusing, location works in an Instagram room, and tagging someone back now actually pings them.
details: The bridge gained a read that returns the group's members. It carries both of the numbers Instagram gives an account — the one a tag is addressed with and the public one — under their own names, because neither can be worked out from the other and confusing them fails silently.
Nora is not in her own room's member list, by design. Instagram leaves the account doing the asking out of it, and counting herself as a member would make her a stranger in her own group.

A member list that cannot be read in full is refused outright rather than returned short. A room that is quietly missing somebody is one the location guard would approve without ever seeing the person it should have refused over.
Tagging back was landed earlier and inert — it needed the member list to confirm someone is actually in the room before it would address them. It is live now.
limitations: Whether an unmapped member in the room blocks a location answer depends on that room's `location` flag, and the flag is ON for the Instagram group this ships into. With it on, an account nobody can name does NOT refuse the answer — it is disclosed and the waiver is counted. An earlier draft of this note said the opposite, which would have told the operator he was protected by a gate he had already chosen to waive.
An Instagram challenge makes the member list unreadable for as long as it stands, and the room-scoped answers degrade to "I can't check right now" until a human clears it.

Because that flag is on, the completeness of this roster is not what stops a location disclosure in that room — only an unreadable roster does. The read stays fail-closed anyway, refusing rather than serving a room short by one member, but the margin is smaller than the code comments claim.

Membership is assumed to arrive whole. The wire carries no cursor and mautrix's own connector treats it as complete, but it has only been observed on a three-person group. Nothing in the code would detect a larger group arriving truncated.
